description: Hi, I'm Rubí! I'm studying Mechanical Engineering. I'm deeply passionate about space, languages, and everything related to mechanics. Outside of that, I'm a writer and illustrator, and I absolutely love the creative field.
summary:
Ghosts of Space is an independent illustrated science popularization mini-book created and illustrated by the Luna de Saturno team (Leslie Rubí Valtierrez Ramírez / Winter Valiz) for the "Abandoned, Yet Not Forgotten" challenge of the NASA Space Apps Challenge.

Through an approach that combines mechanical engineering, poetic narrative, and art, the book pays tribute to the robots and exploratory vehicles that have fallen silent on the surfaces of Mars and the Moon after completing their missions.

Structure and Content of the Work:

Introduction and Concept: It begins with an original cover, an author biography, a prologue, a table of contents, and a conceptual page featuring a ghost character under the premise "Ghosts can be robots too."

Mars Section: Presents an introduction to the red planet followed by original illustrations and detailed technical fact sheets (launch dates, landing dates, location, planned lifespan, and engineering objectives) for five key explorers: Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Curiosity, and Perseverance.

Moon Section: Introduces the history of lunar robotic exploration along with illustrations and technical descriptions of the MAPP, VIPER, and PROMISE rovers.

Interactive Section: Concludes with a coloring section that brings together all the illustrations of the space explorers in black and white, inviting the reader to interact with science and bring each mission to life.
details: The goal of this project is to create an interactive medium for the reader, which is why it features a coloring book section and a personal demonstration of bringing together my interests in engineering, writing, and drawing.
